subject: Private inference farm: growth scenarios & routing decision log
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gonzales <maria@zephyr.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Private inference farm: initial throughput targets & worksheet

Maria,

Great to sync yesterday. I pulled together a quick worksheet (attached) to get alignment on throughput targets, acceptable latency bands, and networking constraints for the private on-prem deployment you described.

High-level ask: can you confirm the following constraints so we can finalize the sizing model?
- Sustained target: 200 inference requests/sec (avg over 10m) with 95th-percentile latency <= 120ms for standard gen-text prompts (~250 tokens).
- Peak spikes: up to 600 rps for bursts lasting up to 2 minutes.
- Connection egress: your site firewall limits outbound bandwidth to 1Gbps; no external model egress is allowed (data remain in VPC).
- Node inventory you mentioned: 8 x A100 80GB nodes (on-site), management VLAN with 10Gb internal fabric.

If any of those are off, note them in your reply. Attached: zephyr_capacity_workbook_v1.xlsx for the math and a blank network template you can fill.

Proposed next step: internal review of two deployment patterns (conservative vs. aggressive) and then a 30-minute technical walkthrough next week.

Thanks,

Jonas
Sr. Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Attachments: zephyr_capacity_workbook_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Maria Gonzales <maria@zephyr.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Zephyr Infra <infra@zephyr.ai>
Date: Mon, 01 Jun 2026 10:15:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Private inference farm: initial throughput targets & worksheet

Jonas,

Thanks — confirmed details below and added a couple of constraints we didn't call out in the meeting:
- Inventory: 8x A100 80GB available for inference. Management and storage nodes are separate.
- Network: internal fabric is 10Gb between nodes, outbound gateway to internet is throttled to 1Gbps. No outbound data allowed without explicit approval.
- SLA expectation: customer-facing features require p95 <= 150ms; internal batch jobs can tolerate higher latency.
- Burst profile: expected periodic spikes up to ~700 rps during end-of-day processing windows; typical daytime peaks ~350 rps.
- Maintenance window: weekly 2-hour window (Sundays 02:00-04:00) where nodes may be cycled.

Attached: onprem-network-diagram.png and a redacted SOC2 evidence packet (soc2-evidence-redacted.pdf) for your security team.

Happy to join the technical walkthrough. Goal is to finalize routing (inside VPC: direct single-tenant vs. split routing with a hot-cold pool) and a minimal autoscale policy.

—Maria
Infra Lead, Zephyr.ai
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gonzales <maria@zephyr.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 08:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private inference farm: proposed deployment patterns and routing

Team,

Thanks for the details, Maria — that clarifies the burst envelope and network constraints. Quick internal summary and two options for Zephyr to choose from:

1) Option A — Predictable, conservative (recommended for initial go-live)
   - Baseline: reserve 4 GPUs as primary serving pool (steady-state handling ~220rps with batching & KV cache warmed)
   - Hot spare: 2 GPUs in warm standby for rapid scale-up (cold-start warmup ~20–30s)
   - Burst: leverage the remaining 2 GPUs for short spikes via on-node rapid scale (autoscale trigger based on 10s window crossing 300rps)
   - Routing: single-tenant routing inside VPC with prefix caching and per-tenant request queues. No external egress.
   - Expected p95: 110–140ms for 250-token gen depending on batching; peak tail could rise to 200ms briefly without extra nodes.

2) Option B — Aggressive, lower-latency (if Zephyr is comfortable committing more capacity)
   - Baseline: 6 GPUs serving; 2 for burst/maintenance cover. Aggressive batching tuning for low-latency path.
   - Routing: split pools (hot low-latency pool + cold high-throughput pool) with smart router directing small/interactive requests to hot pool.
   - Expected p95: 80–110ms for interactive; much more headroom for spikes to 700rps.

Network considerations
- With 1Gbps egress throttle we limit external telemetry; internal 10Gb fabric is sufficient for KV syncs and model shard transfers assuming we avoid cross-rack saturation.
- We recommend MTU and NIC offload checks; if cross-node transfers push >6Gbps sustained we should spread shards differently.

Operational asks
- If Zephyr has a preferred maintenance cadence (beyond weekly window) let us know — Option B reduces risk during maintenance.
- We will prepare a short simulation runbook (load script + ticketed maintenance) to validate option choice in a test cluster.

Attachments: update in the workbook with preferred option; I'll add a short runbook draft after your pick.

-Jonas
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Private inference farm: routing decision log — next steps

Maria,

Appreciate the quick answers. We captured the two options — Zephyr, if you can reply with "A" or "B" and any hard constraints on weekly maintenance or SOC evidence acceptance, we will:
- Produce a 2-page decision log summarizing expected latency/cost tradeoffs
- Schedule a 30-minute validation run with our load engineer to execute the simulation (we'll bring the runbook and a pre-built load container)
- Prepare a DocuSign for an initial capacity reservation (if you pick Option B we'll include an 8-week early-commit discount)

Ping us with a preferred time for the walkthrough; afternoons PT work best for our load engineer.

Best,
